subject: Degrees of freedom, equality constraint, ordinal data

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Degrees of freedom, equality constraint, ordinal data
parts:
I have a problem where lavaan's degrees of freedom do not match my expectations when variables are declared ordinal, but do match my expectations when variables are not declared ordinal. Here is my script:

## Test for lavaan DF error, equality constraint
makeerrdat<-'
f1 =~ .8*y1
f2 =~ .9*y2 + .8*y3 + .7*y4
f3 =~ .8*y5 + .9*y6 + .8*y7
f3 ~ 0.5*f1 + 0.5*f2
f1 ~~ 0.5*f2
'

errdatcont<-simulateData(model=makeerrdat,model.type="sem",meanstructure=F,std.lv=T,sample.nobs=750,standardized=T)
str(q1dat)

errdatordinal <- as.data.frame( lapply(errdatcont, cut, 4, labels=FALSE) )
str(errdatordinal)

testerrdat<-'
f1 =~ y1
f2 =~ y2 + y3 + y4
f3 =~ y5 + y6 + y7
f3 ~ a*f1 + a*f2
'
testerrord.out<-sem(testerrdat,data=errdatordinal,ordered=c(paste0("y",1:7)),parameterization="Theta")
summary(testerrord.out)

testerrcont.out<-sem(testerrdat,data=errdatordinal)
summary(testerrcont.out)

param.ord<-parametertable(testerrord.out)

## End

     The simulation model has 7 observed variables loading on 3 factors, with one factor having only 1 observed variable indicator. In addition, the two structural paths, from f1 and f2 to f3, are constrained to equality. As I count it, this model has DF = 13 as conventionally parameterized:
unique observed covariances                                        7*(7+1) / 2 = 28
- 2 free parameters per observed                                                     - 14
+1 for single indicator                                                                        +  1
- 1 for the two structural paths constrained to equality                      -   1
- 1 for the free covariance between f1 and f2                                    -   1
                                                                                                             13  DF
     And when the variables are *not* declared ordinal, that is what lavaan reports
 Estimator                                         ML
  Model Fit Test Statistic                      53.443
  Degrees of freedom                                13

     However, when I estimate the same model using the same data but declare the observed variables ordinal, lavaan reports DF = 12, not DF = 13:
  Estimator                                       DWLS      Robust
  Model Fit Test Statistic                       6.191      12.391
  Degrees of freedom                                12          12
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.906       0.415
  Scaling correction factor                                     0.543
  Shift parameter                                                   0.983

     Now I know that parameterization is dramatically different for ordinal variables, but I have understood that, in terms of the overall DF, the differences "all come out in the wash," for a single-group model without specific constraints on the extra parameters.
     I (eventually) use parametertable() to track down the "extra" free parameter. That output appears to show the two structural paths constrained to equality being counted as 2 separate free parameters, if I am reading the "free" column correctly. But this is so for both outputs, so maybe that is not the real source of the discrepancy(?).
     I'd appreciate an assist in understanding what is happening here.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Degrees of freedom, equality constraint, ordinal data
parts: Now I know that parameterization is dramatically different for ordinal variables, but I have understood that, in terms of the overall DF, the differences "all come out in the wash," for a single-group model without specific constraints on the extra parameters.
Not really, just by coincidence in many circumstances, such as when all your factors are at least just-identified.

I (eventually) use parametertable() to track down the "extra" free parameter. That output appears to show the two structural paths constrained to equality being counted as 2 separate free parameters, if I am reading the "free" column correctly. But this is so for both outputs, so maybe that is not the real source of the discrepancy(?).

It is not.  The different numbers for equality-constrained parameters get compensated for by counting the constraints at the bottom of the parameter table (where $op == "==").

The source of the discrepancy is that in ML, your residual variances are free parameters, only one of which must be fixed (for single indicator y1), whereas they are all already fixed == 1 in DWLS.  The thresholds "wash out" (saturated, like mean structure is in the ML case), and here is the count for DWLS fitted to polychoric correlations:

unique observed polychoric correlations                  7*(7-1) / 2 = 21
- 1 free loading per observed (when std.lv = TRUE)                   -  7

- 1 for the two structural paths constrained to equality             -  1
- 1 for the free covariance between f1 and f2                        -  1

12  DF
